item.text: I’ve confirmed the repo is public on GitHub, and the issue list is visible there. Next I’m checking whether the gate terms are defined in repo docs or whether this is a straight issue-to-gate classification problem based on the open issue set.

I have the GitHub connector available now, so I’m pulling the issue bodies directly instead of guessing from titles. That should let me classify the gate coverage cleanly and avoid giving you a fuzzy mapping.

I’ve got two concrete issue bodies already. I’m now sampling the rest of the open issues so I can map them by actual failure mode, not just by title. That should let us decide which ones belong in build, test, drift, routing, or rollback coverage.

I mapped the currently open parent issues I could verify in [vercel-labs/agent-skills](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-skills/issues) to the gate types based on each issue body. This is an inference from the issue descriptions, not an existing label system in the repo.

**Gate legend**
- **Build**: package/release hygiene, artifact validity, repo publishability
- **Test**: validation, fail-fast checks, example correctness, runtime safety
- **Drift**: docs vs reality, stale duplication, provenance mismatch
- **Routing**: discovery, naming, skill selection, task-to-skill matching
- **Rollback**: update/revert path, provenance, lifecycle safety after publish

| Parent issue | Relevant gates | Why |
|---|---|---|
| [#235 Some skills do not match their folder name's](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-skills/issues/235) | Drift, Routing | Frontmatter `name` diverges from folder name, which creates naming drift and can confuse skill selection. |
| [#232 Post-task skill lifecycle management with SkillClaw](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-skills/issues/232) | Drift, Rollback | The issue is about cleaning up duplicated, stale, and fragmented skills over time. |
| [#230 Add LICENSE file](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-skills/issues/230) | Build, Drift | The repo advertises MIT but lacks the license file, so publish/legal metadata is out of sync. |
| [#224 Claude Code plugin using agent-skills for web design guidelines](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-skills/issues/224) | Routing | This is about surfacing the skill through a plugin and making the skill discoverable in the right workflow. |
| [#216 `ssr: false` used without `use client`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-skills/issues/216) | Build, Test | The example is invalid in a Server Component context, so it should fail validation before shipping. |
| [#214 Upload fails with `SKILL.md description cannot contain XML tags`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-skills/issues/214) | Build, Test | The upload artifact is rejected by the platform, so this is a packaging/validation failure. |
| [#207 Add a description to improve Dispatch discoverability](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-skills/issues/207) | Routing | The skill needs a description so external routing/recommendation systems can surface it correctly. |
| [#182 Why there are some files `metadata.json` in skill folder](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-skills/issues/182) | Build, Drift | Unexpected files in a skill folder usually point to packaging hygiene or repository-content drift. |
| [#169 `AGENTS.md` wastes context, restructure for progressive disclosure](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-skills/issues/169) | Drift, Routing | The issue is about duplicated guidance, context leakage, and a routing doc that points agents at the wrong level of detail. |
| [#168 How to update an already published skill](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-skills/issues/168) | Rollback | This is fundamentally about the post-publish update path, which is the operational side of rollback/revision control. |
| [#162 Strict Runtime Environment Checks for Agent Skills](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-skills/issues/162) | Test | This proposes a pre-execution guard that verifies environment constraints before a skill runs. |
| [#156 `npx skills list` should show origin of each skill](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-skills/issues/156) | Routing, Rollback | Provenance helps users and agents trace where a skill came from and safely revert or refresh it later. |

**Short read**
- The strongest **routing** issues are [#235](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-skills/issues/235), [#207](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-skills/issues/207), [#224](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-skills/issues/224), and [#169](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-skills/issues/169).
- The strongest **drift** issues are [#230](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-skills/issues/230), [#235](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-skills/issues/235), [#169](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-skills/issues/169), and [#182](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-skills/issues/182).
- The strongest **build/test** issues are [#214](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-skills/issues/214), [#216](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-skills/issues/216), and [#162](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-skills/issues/162).
- The clearest **rollback** issues are [#168](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-skills/issues/168), [#156](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-skills/issues/156), and [#232](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-skills/issues/232).
